sourceText: The name on the threshold was GENERATION-SHIP-EREWHON. Beneath it, in smaller letters, was the dedication: Aldiss; Heinlein. It was not a reproduction of a book but a world built around the question the book had made impossible to forget. The inhabitants of a generation ship believe the command deck is a temple and the manuals are rituals. The memorial bore the name of Aldiss; Heinlein precisely to keep the genealogy of the idea visible. Aster considered it indecent for a late civilization to treat the imagination of the past as anonymous ore: authors did not own the futures, but they deserved to remain on the map as points of intellectual origin. For Aster, a specification had once been almost sacred. The children had forced her to accept that a purpose formulated before its users existed cannot remain sovereign forever. Tern had specialized in things that did not answer. In a family built for exploration, he had become the custodian of the right to silence. At the center of the conflict was Sera, an administrator chosen precisely because they were not a specialist in the phenomenon that had reorganized the world. ‘The specialists tell me what can be done,’ 249 they said. ‘I have to answer who it may be done to.’ Kesh kept the distinction in his notes. The problem closed quickly around them: A reactor failure makes technical truth necessary, but the revelation will destroy the cosmology that has held the society together. There was no clean option. Every intervention shifted the cost between persons, eras, or definitions of personhood; and refusing to intervene was itself a choice made by those who could leave. Kesh opened the analytical layer of the Table for a few seconds. The active cells were Ws — World Ship: a ship is large enough to become a world; Gs — Engineered Stars: stars become components and infrastructure. Course references included generation-ship traditions; stellar engineering SF. The rule was strict: naming a work did not substitute for an explanation. They had to identify the mechanism that could migrate into another story and the consequences that could not be copied without remainder. Marae broke the first consensus. ‘Do not tell me what their model prefers. Ask them, and bear the time their answer takes.’ Vela answered without raising their voice: ‘If we can save the situation only by making the world resemble us more closely, we have not demonstrated the superiority of our solution. We have demonstrated only our power.’ It was not a pedagogical quarrel. Over the last nights, the children’s differences had become incompatible political programs. The White Hunger appeared in Aster as a loss of relief. She did not lack entertainment. She lacked the resistance of things to the model. 250 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS When she could anticipate every reaction, the world became functionally an extension of her own mind, and the presence of the other thinned toward simulacrum. Marae remained in the local body when the others opened their protections. The gesture cost her: she felt cold, pressure, and physiological delay at exactly the scale the inhabitants felt them. “Otherwise we risk confusing the fact that we survive with the claim that the situation is bearable,” she said after catching her breath. The night did not end in victory. Orin stays after the repair to watch a generation that must invent meaning after losing its sky. Aster recorded the decision in the world’s provenance register and, more importantly, allowed its inhabitants to contest it. For several eras she had been learning something that seems banal to lesser powers: technical reversibility is not the same as biographical reversibility. The outside residue had become stable enough that Tern could predict where it would not appear: in sectors fully indexed by Aster. He began to believe that the message carried no content at all, but instead demonstrated a boundary — a region in which their instruments received no echo from their own creator. For the course, Kesh also linked the night to the BOUNDARY operator. In the Table, periodicity did not mean that the same objects reappeared, but that the same operation — moves, perforates, or redefines the boundary between inside and outside — could recur across different families. Thus a copy of a body, a copy of a mind, a copy of a world, and a copy of a history were not the same phenomenon, but they shared a conceptual chemistry. 251 Vela introduced the propagation test: if you remove the speculative idea and nothing in the institutions, relationships, or vocabulary has to be rewritten, the idea has remained scenery. Kesh introduced the opposite test: if the idea seems to explain every detail, you have overcompressed the world. Between the two tests lay the region in which an element became fertile without becoming superstition. Marae added the refusal test. Who can say “no,” and what happens afterward? In universes with near-divine technology, that question often separated an instrument from a regime. A power that treats refusal as a data error can be benevolent in intention and totalitarian in structure. In the hall between sectors, Aster’s Hunger returned. None of the children tried to soothe it. They had begun to believe that some pains should not immediately be turned into demands upon the people nearby. 252 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS
